newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Virgin Express to enter race for Air Liberte.
newsitem.headline: Virgin Express to enter race for Air Liberte.

text.p: Richard Branson's Virgin Express regional airline will bid for ailing French carrier Air Liberte, chief executive officer Jonathan Ornstein said on Wednesday.
"We will make an offer," Ornstein told Reuters.
Ornstein, who declined to give any details of the bid, said the offer would be made "soon".
Other bidders include Virgin rivals British Airways Plc (BA), through its French TAT unit, and a French/Moroccan group headed by travel group Nouvelles Frontieres chairman Jacques Maillot.

Monday was the deadline for bids for Air Liberte, which went into receivership on September 26, but Ornstein said one of Virgin's advisors had said an offer could be submitted up to 48 hours prior to the final decision.
"So we are pursuing this," he said.

Ornstein said Virgin had already sent a letter to the commercial court at Creteil, southeast of Paris, confirming it was interested but also wanted more time to examine Air Liberte's financial situation.
"The offer period was a week or so, very very short," Ornstein said.

"A bankruptcy situation is one thing. A bankruptcy in France is something else. A bankruptcy in France in the airline industry is yet another thing. It's just a very complex issue and we just asked for some additional time," he said.
"But I don't think we're going to get it," he added.
Ornstein said investment bank Merrill Lynch and a French advisor were assisting Virgin Express in its bid.
"At least now we have some horsepower to help us put something together," Ornstein said.
He said he was familiar with BA's offer but not with that of Nouvelles Frontieres.
BA, which has put 25 million French francs on the table, wants to merge Air Liberte with TAT and safeguard 1,250 jobs out of 1,400.
A third bidder, pilot Fernand Denan of airline AOM, made a 120 million francs offer for Air Liberte but has not yet finalised financing.
Brussels-based Virgin Express, launched in April after Branson bought 90 percent of EuroBelgian Airlines SA (EBA), currently operates 14 Boeing 737 planes.
It expects to make a profit of over $10 million this year on turnover of $200 million and wants to more than double the number of its planes by the turn of the century.
Virgin says it has a 85-percent seat occupancy rate due to fares which undercut normal ticket prices by up to 75 percent.

Air Liberte owns around a quarter of the takeoff and landing slots at Orly, Paris' second-largest airport. It lost 650 million francs in the first nine months of 1996 and has 1.5 billion francs of debt.
